title: Decide when to change course
summary: Strategies need changing when the facts change, but not every quarter. Agree in advance what would make you change course, and test plans for weak points.

beginner: Write down the signals that would show a bet is failing.
Agree them with the sponsor before results come in.
Run a premortem: imagine the strategy failed, and list why.
Fix the biggest risks the premortem found.
Revisit the signals at each review.
intermediate: Separate small adjustments from real changes of direction.
Decide in advance who can change the strategy and how.
Communicate changes clearly, with the reason.
experienced: Spot when the core challenge itself has changed.
Stop sunk-cost thinking about failing bets.
Lead the organisation through a change of direction.

toolExamples.miro: Run the premortem on a shared board.
toolExamples.confluence: Record the change signals with the strategy.

sources.title: Performing a project premortem (Gary Klein, Harvard Business Review)
The perils of bad strategy (Richard Rumelt, McKinsey Quarterly)
